newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian PM says early election plan canvassed.
newsitem.headline: Australian PM says early election plan canvassed.

text.p: Australian Prime Min ister John Howard said on Monday he had discussed with state leaders the possibility of holding an early election to push through his plan to regulate Aborigines' native land title.

Asked whether he had on Monday discussed an a double dissolution, a form of early election that can force government measures past a obstructionist upper house, Howard said: "I think in these sorts of discussions the full gamut of political possibilities is always canvassed."
Howard declined to comment further on the issue.

Senate minority parties are expected to oppose part of Howard's plan to regulate native title, an intractably difficult issue that has set pastoralists against aborigines, who the High Court now says are entitled to some use of grazing land.
But Senate obstruction can arm the constitution's deadlock-breaking mechanism, which involves an early election.
If the Senate twice rejects legislation from the government-controlled lower house, the constitution lets the prime minister dissolve both houses for an election.
After the election, the members of the two houses assemble together to consider the bill. Since government members of the more numerous lower house would predominate, the bill would usually pass.
But the election cannot be held later than six months before the latest possible date for a regular election.
Since the current House of Representatives expires in mid 1999, a double dissolution could not practically be held later than the end of next year.
